context_requirements: Cells must have labile or elevated intracellular metal pools (Cu, Zn, Fe) for chelation to perturb metal-dependent processes.
Metal-responsive transcription factors (MTF1, NFE2L2, HIF1A) must be functional.
Hepatocyte-like lines with high metal handling and metallothionein capacity (HEPG2) respond more strongly.
Cells with low basal metal stress or low metal uptake may show little transcriptional response.
falsifiers: No change in metal-responsive genes (e.g., HMOX1, MT1X, MT2A, SLC11A2) at 24 h in any line.
No suppression of sterol/cholesterol synthesis genes at 24 h.
No oxidative stress or UPR gene induction at 24 h.
Responses identical across all nine lines regardless of lineage or metal handling status.
Clear transcriptional response at 6 h that is not sustained or amplified at 24 h.

evidence.supports: Copper chelation suppresses tumor development and angiogenesis and increases apoptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma models.
Chelating agent administration modulates cadmium-induced apoptotic DNA fragmentation in vivo.
Chelating agent reverses arsenic-induced oxidative stress and caspase 3/9 expression changes.
Zinc chelator TPEN attenuates oxidative stress, inflammation and apoptosis in hypoxia/ischemia models.
